candidate_diagnostics.interpretation_boundary: Unit norm checks cover the explicit fourth scorer block and sampled nonfloored events, not all inputs or training. Diagnostics compare each operation to aligned raw within a checkpoint. Cross-checkpoint match mass and norm differences confound adaptation. Attention mass, centered-score and logit changes do not identify label relevance, validate holdout outcomes or estimate a mediation effect. L1 distances to a shared reference cannot be subtracted to recover the pairwise L1 distance.

observations.statement: Pooled history improves AUC over static features by 0.0052224992; target-aware history adds 0.0031358724 over pooling. Both reduce Logloss. This establishes useful baseline history signal, not a specific semantic matching mechanism.

Full count correction hurts both pooling and DIN. Half correction helps pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC) but not DIN (-0.0002082243); full-corrected DIN is also below ordinary (-0.0001905060). The bounded partial-correction follow-up did not rescue the target-aware branch. All are successful executions with scientific negative outcomes, not failed jobs.

In round 3, removing explicit cross-field products improves both metrics at either context setting. Context-product removal raises AUC but worsens Logloss at either cross setting. The AUC interaction is negative (-0.0002827692), so the joint gain is subadditive. Both restrictions are not necessary for an improvement.

Round-4 replays exactly match their source paths on all reported aggregate and slice metrics. Inline joint matches adapter joint, with zero helper logit discrepancy on the first 512 impressions. Original baseline and ordinary adapter remain different (-0.0000309064 adapter AUC, +0.0000745803 Logloss). This is stable seed-42 path dependence without identified root cause.

Latest normalized aligned candidate has AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067 on 3,234,051 validation exposures (159,437 positives). It leads all 20 supplied trial entries in AUC and all 20 recovered detailed rows in Logloss; repeated rows do not supply independent support.

Aligned normalization improves AUC by 0.0004876568 and reduces Logloss by 0.0001270182 versus raw aligned. Crossed normalization changes AUC by only +0.0000139449 and worsens Logloss by +0.0002459431. A universal benefit from product normalization is not observed.

Aligned beats crossed by +0.0011162489 AUC with raw products and +0.0015899607 with unit products; Logloss also favors aligned in both. Alignment-by-normalization AUC interaction is +0.0004737118 and Logloss interaction -0.0003729613. This differs from round-3 subadditivity because the factors are different.

Latest-minus-original-DIN AUC is +0.0016197051 and Logloss -0.0002312389; latest also improves both metrics versus the earlier context-retaining cross-removal arm. The aggregate AUC/Logloss tradeoff between the earlier joint and context-retaining restriction is no longer a reason to prefer either over the latest candidate at seed 42.

Latest supplied diagnostics report unit product norm 1.0, maximum unit norm error 1.78814e-7, aligned/crossed unit norm difference <=2.38419e-7, zero padding mass, zero empty summary and zero forward/helper logit error on the first 512 impressions. All 60,475 visible valid events are nonfloored in both products. Unit aligned/crossed directions differ (mean cosines -0.02531, +0.00495, -0.00628 in the three trained checkpoints).

Normalization at the aligned-unit checkpoint changes weights, summaries and logits relative to aligned-raw counterfactuals (mean nonempty weight L1 1.59829, summary L2 5.57161, absolute logit change 0.45850). These are diagnostic activity measurements, not counterfactual validation scores or causal mediation. All diagnostic variants are referenced to aligned raw, not each checkpoint active model.

Latest improves both metrics over raw aligned in 21 of 23 supplied slices, but loses both in history_17_64 (157391 samples/6311 positives) and user_train_frequency_100_4294967296 (1004912/33140). It improves AUC and Logloss over original DIN in all 23 slices. It beats crossed-unit AUC in all 23, but has worse Logloss in empty_history, past_pv_absent and the highest frequency bin. These are exploratory overlapping summaries.

Latest recovers the raw-aligned empty-history and pv-absent losses, but zero history summaries mean empty-history changes cannot directly demonstrate better history-event matching; training of shared representations/classifier can change these scores.

All history arms report 17,130,275 parameters (17,078,688 embedding; 51,587 dense). Latest wall/train times are 614.783/524.601 seconds, peak GPU allocation 832,739,328 bytes, throughput 179,887.75 examples/s and whole-batch p95 22.135 ms at batch size 4096 including feature gathering. Latest versus raw aligned increases peak allocation 3.78% and train time 1.94%; versus original DIN increases peak allocation 27.15% with similar train time. Single-run timing does not establish an efficiency frontier.

All 20 trajectory entries report operational success; all 15 directly supplied detailed receipts have null errors. Five older detailed receipts are available only in scoped agent-r0004 memory and are marked as such. No failed host model run is exposed, and no unseen failure is invented.

interpretations.claim: Fixed-width aligned target/history category-brand products may be a useful inductive bias; the matched unit-norm replacement contrast weakens an explanation based solely on the explicit product scalar L2 magnitude.
interpretations.status: Provisional single-seed controlled performance support, conditional on receipt-described isolation; semantic causal mechanism unestablished.

interpretations.claim: Normalization and pairing interact in these observed runs. The aligned unit variant improves ranking and probability loss together, whereas the crossed variant does not obtain comparable benefit.
interpretations.status: Descriptive factorial support at one seed; mixed-round raw corner requires source-equivalence verification.

interpretations.claim: Equal explicit product norm and parameter count do not match coordinate distributions, Jacobians, learned embedding norms in other blocks, optimization, effective hypothesis class or information accessibility. Crossed fields can adapt through training and other blocks retain mixed-field/context signals.
interpretations.status: Alternative mechanisms remain viable; replacement is not an information-null or semantic proof.

interpretations.claim: The current strongest conclusion is improved local validation performance at seed 42. Neither repeated robustness, novel architecture priority, production benefit nor full DIN reproduction is established.

Count-balancing failures remain relevant negative evidence: changing attention mass or a seemingly plausible history bias is not sufficient for useful CTR prediction. Product normalization is a different intervention and does not revive the count-correction branch.
interpretations.status: Preserve earlier revision and abandoned target-aware count-correction trajectory.

prior_work_and_difference.inherited_components: Receipt-described static/history embeddings, target/category/brand/action/recency features, target-aware scorer blocks, masked softmax aggregation, history value representations, classifier, optimizer/loss and training recipe. Source-level claims remain conditional without source access.
prior_work_and_difference.local_algebra: Let q_c,q_b be target category/brand vectors; h_c,h_b history category/brand vectors; u action/recency context. D=q_c*h_c+q_b*h_b (aligned), X=q_c*h_b+q_b*h_c (crossed), C=(q_c+q_b)*u, with * elementwise. Ordinary product block is D+X+C. Round-3 flags form D+(1-A)X+(1-B)C. r0003-cross_only REMOVES X and retains D+C; it is NOT the r0005 crossed replacement, which uses X alone. r0003-context_only removes C and retains D+X. Raw aligned is D; latest unit aligned normalizes D by its per-event L2 norm with an implementation floor; crossed arms replace D by X with raw or unit normalization. Exact floor constant/source is not exposed. Other scorer blocks and history values retain context and learned mixed-field interactions.
prior_work_and_difference.mechanism_difference: Count correction changes s_i to s_i-alpha*log(n_type), affecting between-type attention mass. Product restriction/replacement instead changes one explicit target-history interaction block. Unit normalization changes that block magnitude and gradients; it is neither count balancing nor softmax removal. No supplied trial combines these mechanisms.

primary_sources.inspection: Public primary text inspected in this phase. Candidate-conditioned weighted history aggregation is inherited background; published activation weights omit output softmax. The local softmax reference is DIN-style, not a full DIN reproduction.

Public primary section inspected in this phase. FiBiNET learns field interactions with bilinear parameters; the local fixed-width product restriction/normalization adds no parameters or SENET/bilinear layer.
Registry-only in this phase; prior publisher full-text access failure is missing evidence, not scientific counterevidence. No detailed DMR reproduction or equivalence claim.

prior_work_and_difference.novelty_status: Unverified. A locally mechanism-distinct intervention and bounded background source inspection do not establish literature priority or exhaustive nearest-work coverage, including normalized interaction methods.
prior_work_and_difference.industry_status: External reports with task/split/field mismatches; no claimed local transfer or mandated architecture. No disabled personal knowledge source is invented.

No new adaptive variant follows automatically from this study. If the gain or bridge fails, retain negative results and choose continuation using a new prospective observation/hypothesis record. Do not revive the count-correction sweep based on product results.
predicted_observations: If the selected intervention is robust, aligned unit has positive paired AUC differences against original DIN and aligned raw across the new seeds, with probability-loss tradeoffs and between-seed variation reported.

If the pairing-specific normalization explanation transfers, aligned-minus-crossed is positive under unit normalization and normalization-by-pairing AUC interaction remains positive. Normalization need not help crossed Logloss.

The same-body aligned/raw bridge should preserve parent outcomes if implementation equivalence holds; disagreement is a discriminating implementation finding, not a failed scientific hypothesis to hide.

memory_updates.observation: Normalized aligned is the seed-42 AUC and Logloss leader among 20 supplied trial entries. Relative to raw aligned: +0.0004876568 AUC, -0.0001270182 Logloss; two reported slices regress. No repeated-seed support.
memory_updates.revision: Supersede the provisional incumbent while preserving all earlier raw-parent, count-correction and implementation evidence.

memory_updates.qualification: Single-seed performance contrast conditional on receipt-described source isolation; semantic interpretation remains hypothesis, not repeated support.
memory_updates.observation: Aligned versus crossed at unit normalization: +0.0015899607 AUC and -0.0004220161 Logloss. Scalar product norm is matched in the limited nonfloored diagnostic sample; broader training/coordinate confounding remains.
memory_updates.revision: Narrow the simple scalar-L2 explanation; retain gradient, distribution, adaptation and effective-capacity alternatives. Raw-corner mixed-round isolation remains unverified.

memory_updates.observation: Crossed normalization has near-zero AUC change (+0.0000139449) and worsens Logloss (+0.0002459431); normalization is not uniformly beneficial.

Does the frozen pairing-by-normalization interaction and candidate advantage repeat at paired seeds 43/44 after a verified same-body raw corner? No further identical seed-42 replay or adaptive strength sweep is currently justified.
memory_updates.revision: Latest replacement/normalization controls have been observed; prioritize their robustness while retaining earlier factorial findings. Proposed records are embedded in this authorized output only, not written to human-owned or closed memory.

limitations: Only seed 42 is observed. Replays and inline realizations are correlated lineage evidence, not independent seed or mechanism repetitions. No standard errors, p-values or user-cluster bootstrap intervals can be manufactured from aggregate metrics.

Selection has repeatedly reused open validation. Independent paired seeds address initialization robustness but do not remove validation-selection bias; closed assessment remains unrequested and must follow suite freeze.

No source, raw input, checkpoints, prediction vectors or cluster IDs are exposed. Receipt notes describe prospective local checks and may say untrained even though host receipts now report successful training; the host status and measured validation result govern execution status. Source-level/causal audits are not rerun.

The raw aligned corner predates the three same-body round-5 arms. Round-4 implementation consistency reduces, but does not eliminate, mixed-source concerns. The original-adapter baseline mismatch is preserved rather than silently normalized away.

Unit norms are verified only on 60475 first-512 visible nonfloored events. Equal norms do not fix feature distributions, gradients, effective capacity or other input norms; the entire-population floor rate and actual semantic causal mechanism remain unknown.

The diagnostic sample is ordered and candidate-authored, with few empty and brand-only histories. Cross-checkpoint differences mix intervention and training adaptation. No diagnostic perturbation has an authorized scored performance result.

All slices are exploratory for this analysis: exact training-frequency bin semantics and original prospective definitions are not independently available. Counts are explicit; empty/pv-absent slices have only 310/397 positives. No invented support threshold or slice-based gate is used.

History length/count slices and match diagnostics may use different causal-history windows; model history cap is 128. AUC is not additive over slices, and overlapping slices are not independent contrasts. Missing/unseen-field population slices were not supplied; target-brand-zero diagnostic counts are not missing-field performance estimates.

The latest candidate loses both metrics in history_17_64 and highest training-frequency groups versus raw aligned, and has worse Logloss in three slices versus crossed unit. These remain in the record despite the overall gain.
Static user/ad snapshot dates are undocumented and treated as fixed benchmark attributes. Production point-in-time validity and causal data readiness are not verified anew.
